content.user_title: Build a React Native Project Foundation
content.value_statement: React Native projects need coordinated configuration for tooling, data, testing, and structure. This skill provides a stepwise Expo foundation with examples for each setup area.
actual_capabilities: Outlines TypeScript installation and a strict Expo tsconfig configuration.
Defines a feature-oriented directory structure for application, shared, database, and theme code.
Shows local Expo SQLite and Drizzle initialization patterns.
Provides a small Zustand store example for application state.
Lists Jest, linting, formatting, and verification setup steps.
limitations: Targets React Native projects that use Expo rather than bare React Native workflows.
Provides examples, not a generated repository or automated project migration.
Does not choose dependency versions or validate compatibility with a specific Expo SDK.
Does not cover backend services, authentication, release pipelines, or production monitoring.

use_cases.title: Start an Expo application
use_cases.description: Create a consistent TypeScript, folders, scripts, and test foundation before feature development begins.

use_cases.title: Standardize a team project
use_cases.description: Use the documented structure and verification checklist to align setup work across a mobile team.

use_cases.title: Add local application storage
use_cases.description: Introduce Expo SQLite and Drizzle folders when a prototype needs structured local data.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic foundation
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up the TypeScript configuration and directory structure described by this skill for my new Expo app.

prompt_templates.title: Add local data support
prompt_templates.prompt: Add the SQLite and Drizzle setup from this skill. Explain each file I need to create.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare development tooling
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure Jest, ESLint, Prettier, and package scripts using this skill. Give me a verification checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a complete setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a phased Expo project setup plan using this skill. Include TypeScript, folders, SQLite, Zustand, tests, and validation after every phase.

output_examples.input: Set up TypeScript for my Expo app.
output: A strict TypeScript configuration based on Expo defaults.
Installation steps for TypeScript and React Native type packages.
A check to confirm compilation succeeds.

output_examples.input: Add a feature module for account settings.
output: A feature folder with components, hooks, services, and types.
An index file for the feature entry point.
A recommendation to verify linting and tests after the change.

output_examples.input: What should I verify after setup?
output: The app runs on iOS and Android.
Tests, linting, database access, and state behavior work.

best_practices: Configure and verify one system at a time.
Use Expo-compatible packages and verify their SDK compatibility.
Commit successful setup phases before starting the next phase.
anti_patterns: Do not install every dependency before validating the base project.
Do not use package examples without reviewing package names and versions.
Do not treat the examples as a substitute for testing on target devices.

faq.question: Which projects fit this skill?
faq.answer: It fits React Native projects that use Expo and need an initial application foundation.

faq.question: Does it create files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides commands, configuration examples, and structure guidance.

faq.question: Does it support local databases?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes an Expo SQLite example and a folder layout for Drizzle schema and migrations.

faq.question: Which state library does it demonstrate?
faq.answer: It demonstrates a small Zustand store for local application state.

faq.question: Does it configure testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It lists Jest and React Native Testing Library installation with verification guidance.

faq.question: Can I use it outside Expo?
faq.answer: Some patterns are reusable, but Expo-specific commands and configuration need adaptation for other workflows.
